summary: Rule compiler validation rejects macro templates causing SLA fallback and reporting mismatch
description: Issue summary: During a scheduled config reconciliation, the rule compiler began rejecting a small subset of routing templates that include nested conditional macros. Impact: Affected routing rules were marked INVALID and the router applied default SLA fallbacks for ~1200 internal tickets across us-east and eu-west between 2026-03-13T03:00Z and 2026-03-13T07:30Z. Reporting shows ~1.6K 'unrouted' events and SLA breaches that do not correlate with runtime router logs. Environment: production rule compiler v2.4.1, config-store consul cluster, reporting pipeline v1.9.6. Timeline: 2026-03-13 02:55Z - config-reconcile kicked; 03:07Z - first invalidation alerts from liveness checks; 03:20Z - on-call paged; 04:10Z - temporary rollback to validation rule applied; 05:45Z - reconciliation re-run; 07:00Z - telemetry discrepancy investigation started. Observed behavior: Compiler rejects templates with nested ternary-style macros and emits validation error, router marks rule as INVALID and applies default SLA route. Expected behavior: Compiler accepts templates with supported macro constructs or emits a safe warning and prevents mass invalidation. Partial mitigation: Rolled back the strict validation rule in the compiler and re-applied reconciles for affected stacks. Full resolution pending verification and downstream reporting reconciliation.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create routing template with nested conditional macro: {{#if cond}}{{x}}{{else}}{{#if cond2}}{{y}}{{/if}}{{/if}}
2) Push template via config-store to production reconciliation channel
3) Trigger reconciliation job (manual trigger: infra/reconcile-config job)
4) Observe rule-compiler logs for validation error and router console marking rule INVALID

investigation_notes: Found regression introduced by commit 7b9a2f8 (templates grammar rewrite) that tightened AST validation rules for macros.
Unit tests for macro nesting were removed during the grammar refactor; no regression test caught this scenario.
Router correctly falls back to default SLA when rule is marked INVALID, so runtime behavior is safe but not intended for these templates.
Reporting pipeline categorizes fallback-path events as 'unrouted' because the rule invalidation tag isn't being mapped into the fallback_reason dimension.
Affected set is small (~0.7% of templates) but the reconcile batch size amplified the impact when run across many tenants.
Related config changes were deployed to prod at 2026-03-12T23:40Z via ci/cd pipeline: reconcile-2026-03-12.
resolution: Partial: strict validation rule rolled back to behavior from v2.4.0 and reconcile re-run for affected stacks. Patch merged (PR 2354) to introduce opt-in strictness and a non-fatal warning path for nested macros. Reporting reconciliation job queued to correct 'unrouted' counts. Final verification pending historical recon and audit.
